events.hidden_link: Hydration of Q places the OH on the more substituted carbon (C2), creating a tertiary alcohol with exactly 1 stereocentre, rather than a secondary alcohol with 2 stereocentres.
events.route: P is oxidised by PCC to aldehyde Q. Hydration of Q gives R, where the OH is at the more substituted carbon (forming a tertiary alcohol). R has only 1 stereocentre. S is formed by chlorination of R with SOCl2, retaining the 1 stereocentre. T is formed by oxidising the aldehyde in S to a carboxylic acid. U is the methyl ether of R. V is the syn-dihydroxylation product of Q.
events.student_must_notice: The regioselectivity of the hydration of Q to R determines the number of stereocentres and the type of alcohol formed.
events.trap: Students might predict anti-Markovnikov hydration yielding a secondary alcohol with 2 stereocentres, leading to incorrect stereoisomer counts for R, S, T, and U.

members.name: granite-4.2-8b
members.working:
Step 1: Identify P = 2-(hydroxymethyl)cyclohex-2-en-1-one. Structure: cyclohex-2-enone with CH2OH at C2.
Step 2: P --[PCC, CH2Cl2]--> Q. PCC oxidizes primary alcohol to aldehyde, no reduction of ketone. So Q = 2-(methoxymethylene?) Actually hydroxymethyl becomes aldehyde: CH2OH -> CHO. So Q = 2-(methoxymethylene?) Wait: 2-(hydroxymethyl)cyclohex-2-en-1-one -> after oxidation of CH2OH to CHO gives 2-(methoxymethyl?) No, CH2OH -> CHO gives 2-(methoxymethyl?) Actually CH2OH attached to C2 of cyclohex-2-enone; oxidation gives aldehyde at C2: cyclohex-2-en-1-one with CHO at C2 (i.e., 2-(formyl)cyclohex-2-en-1-one). So Q = 2-formylcyclohex-2-en-1-one.
Step 3: Q --[dil. H2SO4]--> R. Dilute sulfuric acid likely induces acid-catalyzed hydration of the alkene? Or rearrangement? For enone with aldehyde, acid may cause conjugate addition? Probably leads to formation of a carbonyl addition product? Might give cyclohex-3-en-1-one? Actually acid could protonate carbonyl and open double bond leading to carbocation and addition of water? But no water mentioned. Likely acid-catalyzed cyclization to give a hemiacetal? However typical sequence: PCC oxidation then acid-catalyzed hydration of alkene to give alcohol. So R likely a cyclohexanol derivative with aldehyde? Might give 2-(hydroxymethyl)cyclohex-3-en-1-one? Not sure.
Given limited time, evaluate statements qualitatively:
(1) R gives immediate turbidity with Lucas reagent at RT. Lucas reagent tests for secondary/tertiary alcohols; immediate turbidity indicates tertiary alcohol. Likely R has a tertiary alcohol after acid addition, so true.
(2) Total number of stereoisomers for S is 4. S is from R with SOCl2/pyridine converting alcohol to chloride; may create chiral center at carbon bearing Cl and carbonyl; could have two enantiomers plus maybe cis/trans? Possibly 2 stereocenters leading to up to 4? plausible true.
(3) T contains exactly 1 stereocentre. T from S via Tollens' (oxidize aldehyde to carboxylic acid) then H3O+. Likely forms a chiral center at carbon bearing former aldehyde? Might be 1, true.
(4) U contains exactly 2 stereocenters. U from R with CH2N2 (diazomethane) methylation? CH2N2 adds CH2 across double bond giving methylene? Could create two new stereocenters. Likely true.
(5) V gives positive Tollens' test. V from Q with OsO4/NMO dihydroxylation of alkene; gives vicinal diol with carbonyl? OsO4 adds across double bond to give cis-diol; no aldehyde formed, so negative. False.
(6) T produces brisk effervescence with NaHCO3. T likely carboxylic acid, which reacts with NaHCO3 to give CO2, brisk effervescence. True.
Thus correct statements likely (1),(2),(3),(4),(6) =5? But (2) maybe not 4. Given uncertainty, answer count =5? Choose 5.

members.name: glm-5.3-flash
members.working: P (2-(hydroxymethyl)cyclohex-2-en-1-one) → PCC oxidizes CH2OH to CHO: Q = 2-formylcyclohex-2-en-1-one. Q + dil. H2SO4: Michael-type hydration of the enone double bond gives R = 3-hydroxy-2-formylcyclohexanone (secondary alcohol + aldehyde + ketone; stereocentres at C2 and C3). R + SOCl2/pyridine: OH→Cl, S = 3-chloro-2-formylcyclohexanone (2 stereocentres, no symmetry → 4 stereoisomers; statement 2 TRUE). S + Tollens/H3O+: aldehyde oxidized to COOH, T = 3-chloro-2-oxocyclohexanecarboxylic acid — still 2 stereocentres (statement 3 FALSE), and as a carboxylic acid it effervesces with NaHCO3 (statement 6 TRUE). R + CH2N2/HBF4: ring expansion of the ketone gives U, a cycloheptanone bearing CHO and OH on adjacent carbons — exactly 2 stereocentres (statement 4 TRUE). Q + OsO4/NMO: syn dihydroxylation of the C2=C3 bond gives V = 2-formyl-2,3-dihydroxycyclohexanone, which retains the aldehyde → positive Tollens' test (statement 5 TRUE). R's alcohol is secondary, so Lucas reagent gives turbidity only slowly, not immediately (statement 1 FALSE). Correct statements: 2, 4, 5, 6 → 4.
